considered_not_activated.decision: Existing Codex maintenance task already owns material upstream detection. Avoid another schedule, writer and provider billing route; no engine activated, authorized new model spend is zero.
Reuse maintained examples if a demonstrated gap justifies gh-aw; no imported workflow or duplicate recurring writer.
Custom catalog managers are a future option; no demonstrated independent gap beyond the existing catalog owner. Dependabot alone owns Action pin proposals.

Not activated for this repository's Python pins. Dependabot's pip ecosystem discovers ordinary requirements/lock files by name; the checksum lock actually used is .github/requirements-ci.lock, a name it does not recognize, and four of five pinned CI binaries (actionlint, gitleaks, syft, grype) are curl-downloaded release tarballs with no manifest it parses at all. catalog-freshness.yml's new pin-drift table already covers all five (plus nautilus_trader) against each tool's latest upstream release. Precondition to revisit: rename .github/requirements-ci.lock to a Dependabot-discoverable name.

Not activated. Default CodeQL setup needs security-events: write (every workflow here is contents: read only) and pins no exact CodeQL bundle version by default, violating this repository's no-floating-pin practice. The scannable surface is stdlib-only Python and a handful of .mjs files with no served application, input boundary or authentication code. Re-evaluate on a served application path (e.g. a hosted dashboard).
